sections.label: MediShield Life coverage expansion
sections.summary: MOH announced MediShield Life coverage would be expanded to new outpatient treatments and home-based medical care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Last month, the Ministry of Health (MOH) announced that MediShield Life's coverage would be expanded to new outpatient treatments and home-based medical care.

sections.label: MediShield Life Amendment Bill objectives
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to amend the Act for three objectives: support coverage expansion, strengthen premium recovery, and improve scheme administration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In view of these developments, the MediShield Life Scheme (Amendment) Bill, or the Bill for short, seeks to amend the Act to achieve three objectives: (a) support expansion of coverage to new models of care; (b) strengthen provisions to support premium recovery efforts; and (c) improve scheme administration.

sections.label: Approved medical institution treatment requirement
sections.summary: Clause 3 amends section 3(1) so MediShield Life can cover treatment or services received from an approved medical institution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Today, section 3(1) of the Act requires the insured to receive treatment or services in an approved medical institution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, going forward, clause 3 of the Bill amends section 3(1) to enable MediShield Life to cover medical treatment or services received by the insured, as long as it is from an approved medical institution.

sections.label: Scoped approvals framework
sections.summary: Clause 4 introduces new sections 3A and 3B setting out the framework for scoped approvals and their suspensions and revocations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This will allow MediShield Life to support patient access to new models of care whilst ensuring appropriate use of MediShield Life Fund monies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 4 of the Bill introduces the new sections 3A and 3B which set out the framework for scoped approvals, and suspensions and revocations of such approvals.

sections.label: HVRSS approval conditions
sections.summary: MediShield Life will cover HVRSS only where a medical institution is approved for the service and conditions are met.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: For example, while HVRSS will be an approved medical service from late 2025 onwards, it does not follow automatically that all providers will be able to make MediShield Life claims for it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MediShield Life will only cover HVRSS where a medical institution has been approved in respect of the service for the purposes of MediShield Life, and if the service is provided in accordance with the conditions of that medical institution's approval.

sections.label: Service of demand notes
sections.summary: The Act will be amended to recognise different modes of serving demand notes and other documents on a defaulter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It notifies defaulters of their owed premiums and of the time by which these must be paid before further measures are taken.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We will amend the Act to recognise the different modes through which demand notes and other documents, are served on a defaulter.

sections.label: Deletion of section 34(2)(k)
sections.summary: Clause 11 deletes section 34(2)(k) of the Act, including serving through additional modalities such as digital means to improve operational efficiency and streamline premium recovery actions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: With those new sections, section 34(2)(k) of the Act is no longer necessary and will be deleted by clause 11.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This would include serving them through additional modalities such as digital means, which will improve operational efficiency and streamline premium recovery actions for the recovery bodies.

sections.label: Access to means information
sections.summary: Clause 9 amends section 28 to broaden access and use of means information to assess whether premium recovery and enforcement measures should be exercised on premium defaulters with lesser means.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To support this, clause 9 of the Bill amends section 28 to broaden the scope for access and use of means information to assess whether premium recovery and enforcement measures under Part 3 of the Act should be exercised on premium defaulters with lesser means.

sections.label: Specifying premium amounts
sections.summary: Clause 5 amends section 4 to allow premiums payable for each insurance period to be specified in a prescribed manner, including a website, with consequential amendments by clause 11.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There is scope to enable premium amounts to be more conveniently accessed by Singaporeans as well as to streamline the administrative process by reflecting premium revisions for operational efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Therefore, going forward, clause 5 will amend section 4 to allow the amount of premiums payable for each insurance period to be specified in a prescribed manner, including a website, with consequential amendments made by clause 11 to section 34(2).

sections.label: Birth anniversary for individuals
sections.summary: The birth anniversary for these individuals will be taken as 1 March in non-leap years and 29 February in leap years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Going forward, the birth anniversary for these individuals will be taken to be on 1 March in non-leap years, and on 29 February in leap years.

sections.label: Expanding scope of offences
sections.summary: The scope of such offences will be expanded to include cases where information provided may affect the amount of grants, subsidies or benefits paid or given to an individual.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: However, such information may also impact the payment of benefits under MediShield Life, as well as the disbursement of premium subsidies or APS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Therefore, the scope of such offences will be expanded to include cases where the information provided may affect the amount of grants, subsidies or benefits to be paid or given to an individual.

sections.label: Expansion of MediShield Life coverage
sections.summary: The proposed expansion of MediShield Life coverage and benefits manages healthcare costs, makes them more affordable, and includes higher claim limits, new benefits and new therapies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed expansion of MediShield Life coverage and benefits will manage healthcare costs especially for larger bills and make them more affordable for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The higher claim limits for hospitalisation and inpatient care as well as existing outpatient treatments, the inclusion of new benefits to cover additional outpatient treatments including mental health, community and home-care treatments, and the extension of MediShield Life coverage to new, potentially life-saving therapies that are proven safe, clinically and cost effective such as Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy Products, recognise and provide for the shifts in healthcare and patient needs especially for larger bills.

sections.label: MediShield Life deductibles and subsidies
sections.summary: The amendment includes premium assistance for lower- and middle-income older individuals, but also raises inpatient deductibles and adds a $500 outpatient deductible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While the proposed amendment includes premium assistance provided to the lower- and middle-income individuals in older age groups, the recommendations do include an increase to inpatient deductibles and the introduction of a new outpatient deductible of $500.

sections.label: Deductibles and financial strain
sections.summary: Patients must pay deductibles before MediShield Life payouts, and the proposed increases may strain the unemployed or those with low MediSave balances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Before patients can claim for MediShield Life payouts, they need to pay deductibles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, while deductibles are an important feature to manage, as I said, the overuse and can be paid with MediSave, the proposed increase for inpatient deductibles and the introduction of a new outpatient deductible may place a financial strain for some, for example, for those who are unemployed and have no income or low balances in their MediSave.

sections.label: Outpatient shift and specialist appointments
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for consideration given more outpatient treatments, and notes feedback that public hospital specialist appointments can take months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I know this is a very difficult decision because at the end of the day, it is about over-consumption as well as coverage, but I hope that some serious consideration can be given to that, especially now that more treatments are outpatient, moving towards outpatient treatments given the improvements in medical technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I have also received feedback from our residents – and it was also reported in Forum of The Straits Times in August this year – that getting appointments to see specialists at public hospitals may take time, sometimes as long as a few months.

sections.label: Premium increases and subsidy eligibility
sections.summary: Premiums will rise about 22% on average, capped at 35% over three years, and the speaker asks MOH to review subsidy eligibility for certain lower- and middle-income individuals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the higher claim limits, expansion in coverage and increased benefits, premiums will increase and there will be a cap on the average about 22% on average with a cap of up to 35% over the three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the Enhanced Mean-Tested Premium Subsidies for Singapore Citizens, I would like to ask MOH if they would review and consider eligibility for the lower- and middle-income individuals who live in properties with annual value (AV) greater than $25,000 but do not own the property they live in or any other property?

sections.label: Healthpoints premium discount pilot
sections.summary: A proposed pilot would let those over 40 redeem premium discounts with Healthpoints via the Healthy 365 app, which the speaker calls a good nudge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed pilot to allow those over 40 years of age to redeem premium discounts with Healthpoints via the Health Promotion Board's (HPB's) Healthy 365 app is a refreshing approach and a good nudge to promoting a healthy lifestyle.

sections.label: MediShield Life subsidy tiers
sections.summary: MediShield Life subsidies consider per capita household income and residence annual value, with no subsidy above $25,000 except for Pioneer or Merdeka Generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MediShield Life premium subsidies now consider both per capita household income (PCHI) and the AV of one's residence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The AV tiers provide the highest subsidy to lower income insured persons living in properties with AVs of up to $21,000 and a reduced subsidy for AVs between $21,000 and $25,000, while AVs above $25,000 receive no subsidy, unless they are from the Pioneer or Merdeka Generation.

sections.label: Removing AV means-testing for subsidies
sections.summary: Urges removing AV as a means-testing criterion, or at least allowing those with AVs above $25,000 to apply for premium subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For retirees and other low-income households, I urge the Government to consider removing AV as a means-testing criterion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minimally, those with AVs above $25,000 should still be allowed to apply for premium subsidies, and a holistic and transparent assessment should be made based on their individual circumstances.

sections.label: MediShield Life Council 2024 review
sections.summary: Says the Council's 2024 review recommendations are timely in keeping co-insurance and deductibles affordable amid healthcare shifts and medical advances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recommendations and inputs of the MediShield Life Council in its 2024 review are timely in ensuring co-insurance and deductibles in MediShield Life remain affordable for Singaporeans, while considering the shift in healthcare delivery from hospital care to outpatient and home-based care, as well as the advances in medical technologies.

sections.label: Broadening MediShield Life provider definitions
sections.summary: Referring to Healthcare Services Act 2020 licensees broadens eligible providers, and refreshed outpatient claim limits fully cover nine in 10 subsidised bills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: By referring healthcare providers to those licensed under the Healthcare Services Act 2020, the new definitions broaden the range of providers, such as outpatient facilities, community care providers and potentially, even home-based medical care that will be eligible for MediShield Life coverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This allows patients to benefit from outpatient facilities as outpatient claim limits are also refreshed to fully cover nine in 10 subsidised bills.

sections.label: Tiered outpatient co-insurance structure
sections.summary: States MOH will introduce a tiered co-insurance structure of 3% to 10% for outpatient treatments, mirroring inpatient or day surgery co-insurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Besides deductibles, I also understand that MOH will be introducing a tiered co-insurance structure ranging from 3% to 10% for outpatient treatments, which mirrors the current co-insurance component for the inpatient or day surgery care.

sections.label: Support for lower-income seniors' premiums
sections.summary: Asks how MOH will support lower-income seniors with minimal MediSave, supports the $80 million APS, and asks for proactive identification of those with insufficient MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the Government has assured us that measures are in place to mitigate these changes, I would like to understand more about how MOH plans to better support our lower-income seniors, especially those who may have minimal MediSave balances in the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I fully support the Government's allocation of an APS amounting to $80 million, as it will provide critical support to those who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies or those who lack family support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Additionally, given that some seniors may face challenges in navigating the application process, can there be a proactive system to identify those who will have insufficient MediSave funds for auto-inclusion for the APS?

sections.label: Premium discounts for healthier lifestyles
sections.summary: Welcomes the Government accepting the Council's recommendation to pilot premium discounts for healthier lifestyles, such as through Healthpoints in Healthy 365.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On various occasions, many of my colleagues in this House, have shared their views on how we can incentivise residents to take up preventive care measures by offering incentives or premium discounts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has accepted the Council's recommendation to pilot offering premium discounts to those who lead healthier lifestyle, such as through Healthpoints in the HPB's Healthy 365 programme.

sections.label: Outcome-based subsidy for chronic conditions
sections.summary: The speaker suggests an outcome-based subsidy model for people with chronic conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Furthermore, I would like to suggest an outcome-based subsidy model for those with chronic conditions.

sections.label: Support for MediShield Life Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the MediShield Life Scheme (Amendment) Bill despite considerations raised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my considerations raised, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the MediShield Life Scheme (Amendment) Bill.

sections.label: Minister approval for medical treatments
sections.summary: Medical institutions must now seek the Minister's approval to provide specific medical treatments eligible under the MediShield Life Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Medical institutions must now seek approval from the Minister to provide specific medical treatments eligible under the MediShield Life Scheme.

sections.label: Premium publication and false information offences
sections.summary: Clause 5 allows premiums to be published online with rates varying by risk profiles, and clause 6 expands offences for false information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amendments to clause 5 will allow for premiums to be published online for transparency, with rates varying by insured persons' risk profiles and needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, clause 6 will expand scope of offences for false information to ensure accountability in health declarations and protect MediShield Life from abuse.

sections.label: Timelines for treatment coverage applications
sections.summary: The speaker asks what the specific timelines are for approving or rejecting medical institutions' applications for treatment coverage under MediShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, what are the specific timelines for approval or rejection of applications by medical institutions for treatment coverage under MediShield Life?

sections.label: Financial sustainability of MediShield Life
sections.summary: The speaker focuses on the amendments' impact on MediShield Life's financial sustainability, saying flexibility can increase access to treatments and coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Today, I would like to focus on just one critical issue raised by these amendments: the impact on financial sustainability of MediShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This flexibility can increase access to necessary treatments and provide coverage for services that better meet patients' changing healthcare needs.

sections.label: Mental health services MediShield Life
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry to consider mental health services within MediShield Life in future evaluations as demand grows.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While the current amendments allow for the inclusion of more institutions and services, I ask the Ministry to consider mental health services within MediShield Life in future evaluations, especially as demands for these services grow.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For instance, including private hospitals offering specialised treatments, such as advanced cancer therapies, could lead to high demand and increased claims under MediShield Life.

sections.label: Financial sustainability of MediShield Life
sections.summary: The speaker says financial sustainability is crucial so premiums stay affordable, and proposes three key steps.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, in our effort to expand this coverage, it is crucial for us to ensure the financial sustainability of the MediShield Life scheme, so that premiums remain affordable for all citizens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I have proposed three key steps to achieve this goal: firstly, establishing clear criteria for essential services; secondly, implementing regular financial reviews; and thirdly, considering sustainable ways to include mental health services in MediShield Life.

sections.label: MediShield Life since 2015
sections.summary: Since 2015 MediShield Life has given all Singaporeans universal lifelong basic protection against large healthcare bills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since 2015, MediShield Life as a national health insurance scheme has afforded all Singaporeans universal and lifelong basic protection against large healthcare bills.

sections.label: MediShield Life 2024 Review principles
sections.summary: The passage notes the Council's four anchoring principles and that the Government accepted recommendations for progressive implementation from April 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note from the MediShield Life 2024 Review Council report that the principles anchoring MediShield Life continue to be: one, coverage for all, for life; second, protection against large medical bills, of course sized at the level of and for public healthcare; third, collective responsibility through risk-pooling at a national level; and fourth, affordable premiums with additional support for target groups and a clear commitment that no one will lose MediShield Life coverage because of an inability to pay premiums.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also note that the Government has accepted the MediShield Life Council's recommendations for the MediShield Life 2024 Review and intend for the changes to be implemented progressively from April 2025 onwards.

sections.label: Shifting care to outpatient settings
sections.summary: The passage anticipates broader private sector participation as coverage expands to new outpatient and home-based treatments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, as we increasingly consider the shifting of care from inpatient settings to outpatient, to home and to community settings and part of these are already articulated in the MediShield Life Council 2024 report, one can reasonably anticipate an even broader-based participation from private sector medical practitioners, not just those anchored in private hospitals but also potentially those working in home-based, in primary care and in community settings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is especially with the MediShield Life Council report recommending expanding coverage to include new outpatient treatments and home-based medical care, such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, home ventilation and respiratory support services and outpatient parenteral antibiotic therapy.

sections.label: Impact on private medical practitioners
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about cumulative regulatory changes disproportionately affecting smaller private clinic entities, who are about a third of registered practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I am also concerned about the cumulative impact of regulatory and legislative changes being done in relative quick succession and how they are affecting private medical practitioners of smaller and singular clinic entities disproportionately.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is notable that the number of private sector medical practitioners are not insignificant and based on the Singapore Medical Council's 2023 Annual Report, they make up about a third of all registered medical practitioners in Singapore, as of December 2023.

sections.label: Premium rates prescribed manner
sections.summary: The Bill proposes that premium rates be specified in a prescribed manner, which may include a website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes that premium rates be specified in a prescribed manner, which may include a website.

sections.label: Elderly access to premium information
sections.summary: The passage asks how elderly residents uncomfortable with online resources will access premium rates and whether both online and offline channels should be mandated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will elderly residents who may not feel comfortable navigating online resources, access and understand their premium rates?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What safeguards will be implemented to ensure they receive adequate notice of any premium changes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Should we not mandate both online and offline channels for premium information to ensure accessibility, transparency and fairness for all Singaporeans, regardless of their digital skills?

sections.label: MediShield Life Council recommendations accepted
sections.summary: The Government has accepted the MediShield Life Council's recommendations and will make three changes to the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The Government has accepted the recommendations made by the MediShield Life Council and we will be making three changes to the scheme.

sections.label: Premium increase and government support
sections.summary: The Government will provide $4.1 billion in support measures over three years, more than offsetting the $1.8 billion total premium increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: With the enhancements in coverage, it is inevitable that premiums have to go up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: However, the Government is committed to helping Singaporeans manage the premium increase and will provide an additional $4.1 billion in support measures, comprising MediSave top-ups and premium subsidies, for the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This will more than offset the total increase in premiums of $1.8 billion over the same period.

sections.label: Coverage and psychiatric ward limits
sections.summary: Coverage expands to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for depression, and psychiatric ward limits rise about 40%, from $160 to $230 per day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This includes expansion of coverage to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation, which is used to treat depression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will also be raising the MediShield Life psychiatric ward limits by about 40%, from $160 per day to $230 per day.

sections.label: MediSave top-ups for seniors
sections.summary: Seniors receive additional MediSave top-ups, including higher Pioneer Generation top-ups, Majulah Package enhancements, and bonuses for lower-balance Young Seniors and Merdeka Generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Seniors, including those with lower MediSave balances, will also benefit from additional MediSave top-ups provided by the Government, which can be used to pay their MediShield Life premiums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These include an increase in MediSave top-up for the Pioneer Generation by up to $300, bringing their maximum annual top-up to $1,200; an enhancement of the one-time MediSave Bonus under the Majulah Package for Young Seniors by $500; and an additional MediSave Bonus of $500 for Young Seniors and the Merdeka Generation with lower MediSave balances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Lower-income Singaporeans who require more support paying for the premiums after subsidies and top-ups may also be invited to apply for APS, which will fully cover their premiums for the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: With this package of support, most seniors, regardless of income, will have their premium increases fully offset over the next three years.

sections.label: Premium increases and support package
sections.summary: Premiums will rise, but a support package offsets increases for over nine in 10 Singaporeans over three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Premiums will need to go up, but we have provided a significant package of support that offsets premium increases for more than nine in 10 Singaporeans over the next three years.

sections.label: MediShield Life coverage review
sections.summary: The MediShield Life Council will review coverage and recommend whether the scheme should cover treatments under these models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The MediShield Life Council will review the coverage of MediShield Life from time to time and recommend to the Government if it would be appropriate for the scheme to cover treatments and services offered under these models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This Bill will provide flexibility for MediShield Life to cover such treatments and services in future, where we so decide to, which will allow patients to make claims for these treatments and services.

sections.label: Existing medical institution approvals
sections.summary: Medical institutions with existing approvals can be approved for existing licensable services, so existing patients' care is not expected to be disrupted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Unless there are extenuating circumstances, medical institutions that have existing approvals as of the date immediately before the amendments come into effect, can be approved in respect of approved medical treatment or services that are or are part of their existing licensable healthcare services and respective service delivery modes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Hence, to address Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Neil Parekh's concerns about continuity of care, we do not expect the care of existing patients to be disrupted by this transition.

sections.label: Suspending or revoking approvals
sections.summary: The amendments allow the Minister for Health to suspend or revoke approval for a specific medical treatment or service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The amendments, however, will allow the Minister for Health to suspend or revoke the approval given in respect of a specific medical treatment or service provided by a medical institution.

sections.label: Claims before suspension or revocation
sections.summary: Claims for treatment or services provided before suspension or revocation will continue to be processed without issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Claims made by patients for such treatment or services provided before the suspension or revocation will continue to be processed without issue.

sections.label: Conditions and grounds for approval
sections.summary: Conditions of approval will be clear to medical institutions, with grounds for suspension or revocation including fraudulent approval or revoked licences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: To Mr Neil Parekh's question, the conditions of approval will be made clear to medical institutions and we have provided clear grounds for when approvals may be suspended or revoked under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These include circumstances where the approval has been obtained fraudulently or if the licence granted to the medical institution under the Healthcare Services Act 2020 to provide the licensable healthcare service that the approved medical treatment or services is or is a part of has also been revoked or suspended.

sections.label: Premium default rate low
sections.summary: The premium default rate, total premium debt as a proportion of total premiums payable, has remained below 1%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Over the years, the premium default rate, which is the total premium debt as a proportion of total premiums payable, has remained low, below 1%.

sections.label: Serving demand notes electronically
sections.summary: The Bill provides for demand notes to be served via email and empowers the Minister to allow service via existing electronic service platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This maximises the likelihood that recovery bodies can serve demand notes on defaulters who do not maintain a valid postal address.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will leverage on two additional avenues: one, the Bill will provide for demand notes to be served via email; two, the Bill will also empower the Minister to make regulations to allow demand notes to be served via existing electronic service platforms.

sections.label: APS premium coverage
sections.summary: Individuals receiving APS will have their outstanding premiums and premiums for the next two policy years fully covered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Individuals receiving APS will have their outstanding premiums, as well as premiums for the next two policy years fully covered.

sections.label: MediShield Life premium schedule website
sections.summary: An amendment allows the MediShield Life premium schedule to be specified on a website rather than in legislation, with policyholders still receiving premium notification letters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: One such amendment is allowing the MediShield Life premium schedule to be specified on a website rather than in legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: All policyholders will continue to receive a premium notification letter which details their premiums payable and premium subsidy entitlements for a given policy year.

sections.label: MediShield Life objectives and engagement
sections.summary: MOH engages community partners to help Singaporeans understand MediShield Life changes, and the Bill strengthens the legislative framework for protection, medical institution management and premium enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In addition, we fully acknowledge the need to help Singaporeans, especially our seniors, understand the key healthcare policies such as MediShield Life, and changes that are made to them from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, in addition to ongoing efforts to raise awareness and improve public understanding of MediShield Life, MOH is also working closely with various community partners like grassroots leaders and Silver Generation Ambassadors to engage Singaporeans on the recent changes to MediShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The debate has largely focused on how we can ensure that MediShield Life continues to adequately protect Singaporeans against large medical bills, while ensuring that the scheme remains sustainable and premiums affordable for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This has always been our objective from the initial launch and subsequent reviews of the MediShield Life scheme, and the design of the Act which provides us the legislative framework to operationalise it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This Bill will strengthen the legislative framework to help us better achieve these objectives by: Enabling MediShield Life to provide adequate protection as the healthcare delivery landscape evolves from hospitals to the community and home settings; Providing a clear and robust framework to manage medical institutions participating under MediShield Life to ensure the appropriate use of MediShield Life monies, especially as MediShield Life coverage expands to new treatments and services; and Facilitating the implementation of premium enforcement measures to ensure that everyone pays their premiums as part of collective responsibility to one another and to ensure the sustainability of the scheme.

sections.label: Assurance on coverage and support
sections.summary: Coverage will not be lost, enforcement targets those unwilling to pay, and those in dire circumstances will receive support if they cannot pay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On the assurance, actually, we ensure that people will not lose their coverage because of that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But as I explained, the whole thinking behind this is that there is 1% of those that we are not able to recover from and we just want to ensure that out of this, the people who are doing it out of just not wanting to comply and not wanting to actually make payment are then caught out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But for those who are actually in really dire circumstances, the processes that I have earlier mentioned will be able to catch them and will ensure that there will be some support given in the event they really cannot pay because of the difficulties.
